To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a confirmatory bifactors model is a better fit than a traditional factor analysis model for the PDSS-R data and the three-factor model, which was the best fitting traditional model, did not fit the data well enough to be considered an appropriate model.

(1) a multidimensional model is more appropriate than a unidimensional factor analysis to model variance in PDSS data; (2) the bifactor model suggests that the PDSS-R measures both a general sleep factor and three sub-factors (insomnia, motor symptoms, OSA and RBD) and; (3) there were differential associations between the general and specific factors with patient characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the multidimensionality of the PDSS and its variants and suggests that the PDSS-R data may be best described by a multidimensional measurement model.
the multidimensional structure of sleep in PD.
the development of a multidimensional scale for the assessment of sleep problems in PD and suggests that a multidimensional measurement model is more appropriate for data collected using the scales.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
multidimensionality should be considered in the interpretation of the results of studies using the PDSS or the PDSS-RE.
a multidimensional measurement model is more appropriate than the traditional confirmatory factor model for the analysis of data from the PDSS-R.
the PDSS-R is a multidimensional scale, which may be more sensitive to the effects of sleep-related symptoms than traditional unidimensional factor analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a multidimensional measurement model is more suitable than traditional factor analysis to measure sleep disturbance in PD.
a multidimensional measurement model is more appropriate than a unidimensional or traditional factor analysis for the PDSS-R, which is consistent with the conceptualisation of the PDSS-R.
the PDSS-R is multidimensional, and that the PDSS-3 is likely to be multidimensional as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PDSS-R is a multidimensional scale and that the items are not all measuring the same underlying construct.
multidimensional models may be useful to model data generated by these scales.
researchers should be aware that the PDSS and its variants may be multidimensional and should use measurement models appropriate for the data.
